label: Early copy steps (recall 1-2) when the input token is y/r/h/d/1/x (or f/l/p)
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase unit: 99.7% of mass is in the copy phase. It never fires on the delimiter step and almost never in the original phase (only a few steps at orig_idx 7-8). Its activation drops off with copy position: recall_idx 1 (the first fed-back input, orig(0)) carries 66% of mass with a 35% firing rate, recall_idx 2 carries 22%, and later positions fire only weakly (2-6%). Within those early copy steps the identity of the input token matters most. y, r, h, d, 1 and x have 3-4.5x lift, f, l and p are weaker. On recall 1, the six-token set alone gives 96% precision. The top activations (about 0.23-0.25) are all at recall 1 with input r, y, d or x. Other tokens at recall 1 give weak activations, which make up most of the lowest quartile. The remaining mass is small, scattered activations at later copy steps. Dev: P 0.65, R 0.61, F1 0.63, mass recall 0.76. Better read as a graded function of token times copy position than as a crisp boolean.
